newsitem.title: USA: California foreclosure activity increases - report.
newsitem.headline: California foreclosure activity increases - report.

text.p: Foreclosure activity in California edged up in August as lending institutions moved to clear more delinquent mortgage loans from their books, a real estate information service said Monday.

Last month, a total of 13,822 California homeowners were drawn into the foreclosure process, up 6.0 percent from 13,043 in July and up 14.9 percent from 12,033 for August last year, according to DataQuick Information Systems.
Foreclosure proceedings peaked last March when lenders sent default notices to 15,473 homeowners.

So far this year, 110,942 California homes have gone into foreclosure, up 27.2 percent from 87,197 for the same period last year. Most of the increase can be attributed to stricter lending industry policies regarding delinquent loans, DataQuick said.

The increase was strongest in California's central valley, especially Sacramento County, where year-to-date foreclosure activity was up 49.0 percent. San Bernardino County had the most moderate year-to-date increase of 4.1 percent. Santa Clara County experienced a 4.2 percent year-to-date increase.
DataQuick monitors real estate activity nationwide.
